results.title: CoreWeave Raises Prices 25%, but Its Margin Turn Started Earlier
results.author: Olivia Johnson
highlights:
CoreWeave raised prices by approximately 25% across its product configurations in July, citing intense demand, greater customer returns, and higher component costs.

The increase is unusually large for cloud infrastructure sold to sophisticated buyers. Yet the more important detail is its timing. CoreWeave says its operating margin had already improved before the new prices took effect.

That sequence changes the story.

...

CoreWeave disclosed the change during its second-quarter earnings call on August 11, 2026. The company reported rising revenue, improving sequential margins, and near-term capacity that management described as effectively sold out.

...

The sequence matters because second-quarter improvement cannot be credited to prices introduced after the quarter ended.

CoreWeave’s second quarter closed on June 30. The company implemented its broad pricing change during July, according to Chief Financial Officer Nitin Agrawal.

Agrawal said the change included an approximately 25% increase across SKUs, meaning individual service configurations built around different hardware and capacity options. He linked it to current demand and improving customer returns from AI infrastructure.

He also said CoreWeave was passing through component price increases. That explanation positions the adjustment as both a demand response and a way to recover higher input costs.

The underlying event occurred on August 11, when CoreWeave released its second-quarter results and held its conference call. The corrected earnings call transcript confirms the price increase, its July timing, and management’s stated reasons.

highlights:

...

CoreWeave — ~25% list-price increase across SKUs (July 2026)

On its Q2 2026 earnings call (August 11, 2026), CoreWeave disclosed “an approximately 25% increase across SKUs in response to the current demand environment,” adding that pricing and margins for Blackwell and Vera Rubin SKUs were “setting new highs” while prior-generation SKUs sat at or above prior levels. Management described near-term capacity as “effectively sold out” (CoreWeave Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Revenue hit $2.58B, up 112% year over year, on a $104B backlog.

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/hr — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). Treat the exact figures as multiply-reported rather than primary-confirmed.

results.title: CoreWeave verhoogt prijzen met 25 procent | FLOH Solutions
results.author: Alisina Nawabi
highlights:
Nieuws 13 augustus · 00:10 5 min leestijd

# CoreWeave verhoogt prijzen met 25 procent en is op korte termijn uitverkocht

CoreWeave verhoogde in juli alle SKU-prijzen met ongeveer 25 procent en meldt dat de capaciteit voor de korte termijn uitverkocht is. Ook oudere GPU-generaties worden niet goedkoper meer.

...

## Kort samengevat

- CoreWeave voerde in juli 2026 een prijsverhoging van ongeveer 25 procent door over al zijn SKU's, bevestigde CFO Nitin Agrawal op de kwartaalcall van 11 augustus.
- De capaciteit voor de korte termijn is volgens topman Michael Intrator feitelijk uitverkocht, ook voor oudere Nvidia-generaties; een pas getekend A100-contract loopt door tot in 2029.
- De verhoging raakt nieuwe contracten en verlengingen, niet de prijs van een lopend meerjarig take-or-pay-contract.
- Het is de tweede verhoging in twee maanden bij een grote aanbieder, na de circa 20 procent die AWS per 1 juli 2026 doorvoerde op zijn gereserveerde GPU-blokken.

CoreWeave verhoogde in juli de prijzen van zijn hele productlijn met ongeveer 25 procent, zei financieel directeur Nitin Agrawal dinsdag op de kwartaalcall, terwijl de capaciteit voor de korte termijn uitverkocht blijft.

Wie in Nederland AI-rekenkracht inhuurt, krijgt daarmee de tweede verhoging binnen twee maanden voor de kiezen. AWS trok de tarieven van zijn gereserveerde Nvidia-GPU-blokken per 1 juli al met ongeveer 20 procent omhoog, en CoreWeave gaat er in dezelfde maand overheen. Het tarief is niet het enige dat verandert. De klassieke uitwijk bij dure rekenkracht, een generatie oudere GPU's huren voor minder geld, is bij deze aanbieder dicht.

...

De stap raakt de SKU's: de losse producttypes in het aanbod, telkens een bepaald GPU-type met de opslag, het netwerk en de software eromheen. Agrawal zei dat de margeverbetering van het tweede kwartaal nog van vóór de aanpassing dateert, en dat die aanpassing een verhoging van ongeveer 25 procent over alle SKU's inhield. Als reden noemde hij de vraag in de markt en het rendement dat klanten op hun eigen AI-toepassingen zien nu ze verschuiven van trainen naar inferentie. Gestegen componentprijzen rekent het bedrijf daar bovenop door.

Een lopend contract verandert er niet door. CoreWeave verkoopt capaciteit vooral via meerjarige take-or-pay-afspraken, en die prijs staat vast voor de looptijd. De 25 procent landt op nieuwe contracten en op verlengingen. Volgens Agrawal komt er dit jaar maar een klein deel van de vloot vrij voor herverhuur, maar liggen de gemiddelde verkoopprijzen daarvoor op of boven het niveau van een jaar geleden. De contracten die het bedrijf in het tweede kwartaal tekende, dus nog vóór de verhoging, hadden al een bijdragemarge die 5 tot 10 procentpunt hoger lag dan die van recente kwartalen.

...

Ook van die oudere generaties is CoreWeave naar eigen zeggen grotendeels uitverkocht.

Which big GPU cloud is cheapest for H100 and B200? On each provider's own pricing page on November 3, 2026: for the H100, Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour on demand, with Lambda a cent behind at $3.99 on an 8-GPU instance. For the B200, Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x), well under Nebius ($8.50) and CoreWeave ($8.60). results.author: Markaicode Editorial
highlights:
CoreWeave bills HGX nodes by the hour; H100 8-GPU On-Demand is $49.24/node-hr. Path B: $49.24, $4,924, ~$35,945 (Aug 2026).

 Aug 31, 2026

CoreWeave in our knowledge graph: 2 relationships

> Quick Answer: CoreWeave's public GPU cards meter multi-GPU nodes by the hour, not a freestanding single-GPU On-Demand line for HGX H100. As of August 2026 (re-verified September 1, 2026, no change), an NVIDIA HGX H100 8-GPU node lists $49.24 / node-hour On-Demand. The page also shows an Inference Single GPU column at $6.16 / hour that matches $49.24 ÷ 8 — but per CoreWeave's own footnote, that per-GPU rate is gated to CoreWeave inference-platform customers via an account executive, not a self-serve SKU anyone can buy today. Path B (USD, no tax, node-hours only): 1 node-hour → $49.24; 100 → $4,924; 730 (≈24/7 month) → $35,945.20. Spot H100 examples sit near $19.51–$19.71 / node-hr (region-dependent). Committed usage can reach ~60% off On-Demand— Depends / sales.

...

1. The $6.16/GPU-hr figure is not a buyable SKU for most customers. It's a derived planning number (49.24 ÷ 8) and it doubles as CoreWeave's "Inference Single GPU Price," which the pricing page's own footnote restricts to customers enrolled in CoreWeave's inference platform, arranged through an account executive. If you're not on that program, budget the whole node.
2. The primary public meter is the node-hour. HGX H100 / H200 / A100 / B200 cards are 8-GPU nodes (GB200/GB300 NVL72 are 4-Superchip units). Dividing by GPU count is a planning convenience, not an invented single-GPU On-Demand purchase path.
3. Spot is not On-Demand. North America Spot examples for H100 land near $19.71 / hr; Europe near $19.51 / hr—label region and interruptibility before you budget Spot as baseline.
4. Idle burns the full node. A reserved or On-Demand node that sits warm still accrues $/node-hour whether GPUs are saturated or waiting on data.
5. Committed capacity is opaque on the public page. "Up to 60% off On-Demand" is marketing + sales—Path B does not invent an effective committed $/hr without a quote.
6. Storage and networking are separate lines. Object / file storage and optional Direct Connect sit beside GPU compute; Path B scenarios below are node-hour compute only unless labeled.

...

results.title: Is CoreWeave Stock Worth Buying? With Billions in Orders Booked, What’s the Outlook for CRWV? | Gate Blog
highlights:
At nearly the same time, CME Group announced in partnership with Silicon Data that it plans to launch two compute power futures contracts on October 5, 2026. These contracts will track the hourly rental cost indexes for NVIDIA’s H100 and B200 GPUs.

...

CME’s planned compute power futures—Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures and Silicon Data B200 Rental Index Futures—will track the hourly rental cost for GPUs, with each contract representing one month of GPU rental expenses.

CME executive Pete Keavey aptly commented, "Compute power has become the currency of the AI era." Silicon Data CEO Carmen Li added that, in the past, different buyers paid vastly different prices for the exact same GPU compute. Compute futures will provide a transparent, tradable benchmark price.

The logic behind this financialization is clear: when a resource’s spot market is sufficiently large, price volatility is significant, and participants are diverse, the emergence of standardized futures contracts becomes inevitable. Today’s GPU rental market meets these criteria. According to Silicon Data, hourly rental prices for NVIDIA’s H100 have risen from under $2 in January 2026 to nearly $3. The B200’s hourly rate has also climbed from just under $5 at the start of the year to between $5.5 and $5.8. The simultaneous rise in rental prices for both chip generations reflects an ongoing tight supply-demand balance.
